reason: profiles/pi carries pi-sandbox-guard 7ad441f's Pi profile with the protections Agent Guard adds to Pi sessions (docs/DESIGN.md section 11). Every change to a vendored file is in the patch and listed here; test/pi-files.mjs checks both, test/pi-launch.mjs tests differences 1 to 5 and 7, test/pi-commands.sh difference 6 and the corpus difference 8.

LICENSE.note: From b60240a, the pi-sandbox-guard commit after 7ad441f that changed only LICENSE's copyright line, to name pi-sandbox-guard contributors.

added.package.json: Replaces 7ad441f's package.json, whose scripts run the npm deploy, bind and status commands that Agent Guard replaces; keeps the module fields.
added.commands/bind.zsh: agent-guard bind: runs scripts/bind-executable.sh with HOME set to the account home and its path overrides unset; replaces npm run bind.
added.commands/doctor.zsh: The Pi checks of agent-guard doctor, which replace scripts/status.sh and scripts/check-path.sh.

not_vendored.scripts/test-ops.sh: Tests pi-sandbox-guard's npm deploy, status and bind scripts, which Agent Guard replaces.
not_vendored.scripts/deploy-all.sh, scripts/deploy-la: Replaced by Agent Guard's installer and CI.
not_vendored.scripts/status.sh, scripts/check-path.sh: Replaced by agent-guard doctor; the vendored suites do not need them.
not_vendored.test/e2e-demo.mjs: A manual demonstration, not a suite.
not_vendored.config/, docs/, README.md, SECURITY.md,: pi-sandbox-guard's own documentation and repository files.

differences.change: Agent Guard's base write protections, appended after pi-sandbox-guard's rules: the engine folder, OpenCode Guard's engine folder, ~/Agent Guard, ~/Applications/Agent Guard.app, ~/.config/opencode, ~/.opencode, ~/.cc-safety-net except its logs, ~/Library/LaunchAgents and the eight shell startup files, plus the resolved target of each one that is a symlink at launch (engine/launch's rule: it exists and resolves elsewhere), passed as AG_LINK_* parameters with an inert path when there is no link. Every folder above a resolved target, up to and not including /, is pinned with a literal deny, as engine/launch pins them, through 32 fixed AG_PIN_* slots, shared with difference 4's cache roots (unused slots inert); a launch that needs more slots is refused. Fixed slots keep the profile one static file passed with -f, with the paths as parameters rather than generated SBPL text.

A project that is, contains or is inside one of difference 1's folders is refused before launch, beside the preamble's existing boundary and agent-config refusals; all of ~/.cc-safety-net is refused, its logs included. For a folder that is a symlink, a project that is or is inside its resolved target is refused too, since the session would be wholly read-only; a project that only contains the target launches with the target write-denied, as for the shell startup files, whose targets are never refused.

Decision D7, as in engine/profile.sb: (deny lsopen), (deny job-creation) and (deny process-exec) of /usr/bin/open, /usr/bin/osascript, /usr/bin/osacompile, /usr/bin/codesign, /usr/sbin/diskutil, /bin/launchctl and /usr/bin/sudo.

Step 7's protections under Pi's ~/.cache grant, for C = ~/.cache as written, C = its canonical path (AG_CACHE_HOME, resolved after the folders below are created, since Seatbelt checks resolved paths and ~/.cache may be a link) and C = the canonical XDG_CACHE_HOME: writes to C/opencode/packages, C/opencode/node_modules, OpenCode's legacy install metadata C/opencode/package.json, C/opencode/package-lock.json and C/opencode/bun.lock, C/opencode/bin, C/opencode/models.json (each as a subpath) and C/opencode/models-*.json are denied, and C and C/opencode are pinned with literal denies. Every folder above each C, up to and not including /, is pinned through difference 1's AG_PIN_* slots, so no cache root can be moved away by renaming a folder above it, such as the parent of an XDG_CACHE_HOME inside the project. XDG_CACHE_HOME travels as AG_XDG_CACHE_HOME, ~/.cache when unset; a value that is not an existing absolute folder refuses the launch. Before sandbox-exec the preamble creates C/opencode/bin at both roots (mkdir -p, so also C and C/opencode on a fresh account), because OpenCode creates a missing bin at every start and the profile denies that create (docs/DESIGN.md section 9).

User-facing repair text names Agent Guard's commands instead of pi-sandbox-guard's npm commands, which no longer exist after the adoption: the preamble's messages and its binding comment say agent-guard bind instead of npm run bind and drop 'from the repo checkout'; src/index.mjs's FILTER-ONLY warning says to install Agent Guard (agent-guard update, or the one-line installer) and run agent-guard bind instead of npm run deploy:launchers and npm run bind from a checkout; launchers/example-custom's missing-shim message says to install Agent Guard first (agent-guard update, or the one-line installer) instead of npm run deploy:launchers.

scripts/bind-executable.sh runs as agent-guard bind (commands/bind.zsh) instead of npm run bind: its usage, hints and executables.conf header name agent-guard bind; every mode but --show stops when node is not on PATH, which npm run guaranteed; --show also prints the checker Node; --checker-node [PATH] records the analyzer's Node in the extension's .guard-node as deploy-local.sh did (validated outside every sandbox-writable root, a Homebrew Cellar path kept as its opt link, mode 0600; without a path, the node on PATH) and cannot be combined with another mode; an executables.conf or .guard-node that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is refused before it is written. scripts/lib-ops.sh is unchanged.

Step 7f (docs/DESIGN.md section 12): the project agent config deny write-denies all of .opencode instead of .opencode/plugins, OpenCode's config file names (opencode.json, opencode.jsonc, tui.json, tui.jsonc) and .cc-safety-net, anywhere under the project. Without it a Pi session could plant an OpenCode plugin or config that a later OpenCode session in the project loads, or a .cc-safety-net/policy.json that switches off cc-safety-net's built-in rules there. The preamble's PROJECT refusal patterns, kept in step with the folder rules, refuse a project inside .opencode or .cc-safety-net; the file-name rules match only the file itself and need no refusal. Seatbelt checks the resolved path, so the preamble's symlinked-config check also refuses a launch where one of these names in the project or launch folder is a link whose target the session can write, or where a link inside .opencode or .cc-safety-net resolves to a writable place outside it, as it refuses a symlinked .pi or .omp; a link to a place the session cannot write, or to a project path whose own name the profile denies, launches, and one whose target is missing is refused.

Step 7f: the analyzer asks before a git push that rewrites or deletes remote refs: --force and its variants (--force-with-lease, --force-if-includes), --mirror, --prune, --delete, a short option cluster containing f or d, or a refspec starting with + or :, with only Git's global options (such as -C <dir> or --no-pager) allowed before push; quoted and backslash-escaped words count as one, redirections are skipped, and no word crosses a shell separator, which can also end the option. Seatbelt cannot stop a push, and pi-sandbox-guard allowed all of these. A plain push, long options such as --follow-tags and a refspec such as main:main stay allowed.

test_notes: test/pi.sh runs profiles/pi/test/shim.mjs unchanged: its launch cases run the preamble against the account's real home, because its fixtures keep the real directory-service lookup. Since difference 4 they create ~/.cache/opencode/bin in that account when it is missing, as they already create and remove ~/.local/share/pi-sandbox-bindable-* folders.

test/pi.sh runs the analyzer suites (smoke, corpus, adapter, degraded) with the account's home, which corpus.mjs needs, under a Seatbelt profile that denies writes to ~/.pi, so the analyzer's security log is not appended to.

test_edits.change: sb, sb_omp and sb_pi_relocated pass the profile's AG_* parameters with inert values (the cache roots as HOME/.cache), read from the profile, since a missing parameter stops the profile from compiling.

runNestedShim passes the profile's AG_* parameters with inert values (the cache roots as HOME/.cache), read from the profile; the ambient-override refusal case expects agent-guard bind instead of npm run bind.

Ten cases after git clean -fdx: eight push forms that ask (--force, -uf, --force-with-lease=..., a + refspec, a : refspec, -d, --mirror, git -C repo push --force) and two that stay allowed (git push -u origin feature, git push --follow-tags origin main:main).
